papers.title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics
papers.summary: Soft wearable robots have evolved rapidly from proof‐of‐concept devices into promising platforms for rehabilitation, occupational assistance, and human augmentation. As the field matures, its central challenge extends beyond developing softer materials and more capable actuators to integrating sensing, intelligence, and human adaptation into systems that users can wear comfortably, trust, and benefit from over long periods. papers.title: Optimization method for spatial robot arm locking-unit layout based on plant root adaptive growth patterns
papers.summary: Purpose To address the optimization problem of spatial robotic arm locking-unit layout, this study proposes a collaborative optimization method based on the adaptive growth patterns of plant roots. papers.title: Sound2Vision: Generating Diverse Visuals from Audio through Cross-Modal Latent Alignment
papers.summary: How does audio describe the world around us? In this work, we propose a method for generating images of visual scenes from diverse in-the-wild sounds. This cross-modal generation task is challenging due to the significant information gap between auditory and visual signals. We address this challenge by designing a model that aligns audio-visual modalities by enriching audio features with visual information and translating them into the visual latent space. papers.title: Recent advances in multi-agent human trajectory prediction: A comprehensive review
papers.summary: With the emergence of powerful data-driven methods in human trajectory prediction (HTP), gaining a finer understanding of multi-agent interactions lies within hand’s reach, with important implications in areas such as social robot navigation, autonomous driving, and crowd modeling. This survey reviews some of the most recent advancements in deep learning-based multi-agent trajectory prediction, focusing on studies published between 2020 and 2025. papers.summary: Point cloud classification is a fundamental task in 3D vision and robotics, yet effectively capturing local geometric structures while modeling global contextual dependencies remains challenging. papers.summary: Complete coverage path planning (CCPP) is a core enabling technology for autonomous operation and navigation of mobile robots and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). papers.summary: Legibility in human-robot interaction (HRI) is often described as the property of robot motion that enables an observer to confidently and quickly infer the robot’s intent. Mature frameworks exist for generating legible motion in front of static observers, typically by making the robot’s destination apparent as early as possible. papers.summary: Patient behaviors related to pursuing robotic-assisted spine surgery remain poorly characterized. papers.summary: This paper proposes a motion control framework for non-wheeled snake robots in rough terrain that integrates obstacle-aided locomotion using piecewise helixes with an intuitive teleoperation interface. The proposed method consists of a steering and coordination strategy for locomotion using piecewise helixes, along with a teleoperation interface system designed to implement this approach. papers.title: Fishers reward program promoting their role as cleaners of the ocean
papers.summary: Marine litter poses an environmental and socio-economic challenge in European seas, imposing costs on fishers who passively collect waste during routine operations. This study explores reward-based programs to incentivise coastal fishers to collect marine litter, drawing on qualitative evidence from Croatia, Italy, Malta, Portugal, and Spain. The study contributes to the debate on recognising fisheries for their environmental contribution beyond seafood production, framing marine litter removal as a public environmental good requiring policy support. papers.summary: Classical metallography using 2D sections provides reliable information on phase fractions but is limited for the quantitative determination of spatial geometries such as pore shapes, graphite morphology, conductor track geometries, or dendrite structures. papers.title: Quantification and classification of carbon nanotubes in electron micrographs using vision foundation models
papers.summary: Accurate characterization of carbon nanotube morphologies in electron microscopy images is vital for exposure assessment and toxicological studies, yet current workflows rely on slow, subjective manual segmentation. This work presents a unified framework that leverages vision foundation models to automate the quantification and classification of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) in electron microscopy images. papers.summary: Cardiac and lung ultrasound require operators to locate patient-specific intercostal acoustic windows and adjust probe position, rotation, and force to acquire standard views. papers.title: Task Framing Effects on Personality-Based Team Formation
papers.summary: This study examines how task framing influences personality-based team selection decisions. Participants will form four-person teams for an entrepreneurial venture after reading task descriptions that vary in their emphasis on different work approaches. We will analyze whether framing systematically shifts which personality traits people prioritize when selecting teammates, and whether this produces differences in team diversity.
